chunks: And it is narrated from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, who said:

I was sitting with Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام when a man came to him and said to him, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has money owed by me, and he wants to imprison me." So he said, "By Allah, I have no money with me to repay on your behalf." He said, "Then speak to him." He said: so he, عليه السلام, put on his sandals. Then I said to him, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, have you forgotten your iʿtikāf?"

So he said to him, "I have not forgotten, but I heard my father, عليه السلام, narrating from my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, that he said: 'Whoever strives in fulfilling the need of his Muslim brother, it is as though he worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for nine thousand years, fasting its days and standing its nights.'"

key_terms.اعْتِكَافَكَ: your spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.حَاجَةِ: a need or pressing matter requiring assistance
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing in worship during the night
key_terms.يَحْبِسَنِي: to imprison me or detain me over a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for helping fulfill the need of a fellow Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith shows the immense virtue of helping a fellow Muslim in distress, even during a time of personal devotional retreat. Imam Al-Hasan عليه السلام teaches that serving others and relieving their hardship is among the greatest acts of worship. The narration also highlights the ethical balance between devotion to Allah and care for the needs of people.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2108 - It is narrated from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said:

"I was sitting with Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali (as) when a man came to him and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), so-and-so has a debt against me, and he intends to imprison me.'
Imam Al-Hasan (as) said: 'By Allah (swt), I have no money to repay your debt.'
The man then said: 'Could you speak to him on my behalf?'
Imam Al-Hasan (as) put on his sandals.
I said to Imam (as): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), have you forgotten your i'tikaf?'

Imam (as) replied: 'I have not forgotten. But I heard my father (as) narrating from my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), who said: “Whoever strives to fulfill the need of his Muslim brother, it is as if he worshipped Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for nine thousand years, fasting during the day and standing in prayer at night.”'
